'''Iwai''' (磐井, dates unknown - 22nd year of Emperor Keitai [528? <ref group="note" name="NihonShokiChronology"/>]), also known as '''Tsukushi Iwai''' (筑紫 磐井), was a regional chieftain in the early 6th century during the late [[Kofun period]]. His kabane was [[Kimi (kabane)|Kimi]]. 

In the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}}, his name is written as "Iwai"; in the {{ill|Kojiki|ace|Kojiki|ar|كوجيكي|az|Kociki|bcl|Kojiki|be|Кодзікі|bg|Коджики|ca|Kojiki|ckb|کۆجیکی|cs|Kodžiki|da|Kojiki|de|Kojiki|eo|Koĝiki|es|Kojiki|et|Kojiki|eu|Kojiki|fa|کوجیکی|fi|Kojiki|fr|Kojiki|gl|Kojiki|he|קוג'יקי|hi|कोजिकी|hr|Kojiki|hu|Kodzsiki|hy|Կոձիկի|id|Kojiki|it|Kojiki|ja|古事記|ka|კოძიკი|kk|Кодзики|kn|ಕೋಜಿಕಿ|ko|고사기|la|Kojiki|lt|Kodžiki|mk|Коџики|ml|കൊജികി|ms|Kojiki|my|ခိုဂျိခိ|nl|Kojiki|no|Kojiki|oc|Kojiki|pl|Kojiki|pt|Kojiki|ro|Kojiki|rsk|Кодїки|ru|Кодзики|sh|Kojiki|simple|Kojiki|sk|Kodžiki|sl|Kodžiki|sr|Коџики|sv|Kojiki|ta|கோஜிகி|th|โคจิกิ|tl|Kojiki|tr|Kojiki|uk|Кодзікі|vi|Cổ sự ký|zh|古事記|zh_classical|古事記|qid=Q813031|lt=Kojiki}}, as "Tsukushi no Kimi Iwai"; and in the fragments of the {{ill|Chikugo no Kuni Fudoki|ja|筑後国風土記|qid=Q135597604}}, as "Tsukushi Kimi Iwai." While the Nihon Shoki describes him as a Kuni no Miyatsuko of the {{ill|Tsukushi Province|en|Tsukushi Province|qid=Q1206461|lt=Tsukushi Province}}, some scholars suggest this was a later embellishment.<ref>{{Harv|Iwai Rebellion (Ancient History)|2006}}</ref><ref>{{Harv|Iwai (Ancient Clans)|2010}}</ref>

Iwai is known for leading the {{ill|Iwai Rebellion|en|Iwai Rebellion|qid=Q3138004|lt=Iwai Rebellion}}, as well as being one of the rare figures from this era whose tomb has been conclusively identified.

=== Nihon Shoki ===
The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}} states in the 21st year of Emperor Keitai (527?)<ref group="note" name="NihonShokiChronology">The chronology of Emperor Keitai's later years may be three years earlier than recorded due to discrepancies with the Baekje Chronicles (辛亥の変). This shifts the events of 527-528 to 530-531. {{Harv|Iwai Rebellion (Ancient History)|2006}}</ref> that {{ill|Oumi no Kena|ja|近江毛野|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q8011171}} led an army of 60,000 across to {{ill|Mimana|en|Mimana|qid=Q1790223|lt=Mimana}} to restore lands seized by {{ill|Silla|en|Silla|qid=Q28456|lt=Silla}}. Iwai, a Tsukushi chieftain, reportedly accepted bribes from Silla to block this mission and gained control over trade routes.<ref>{{Harv|Iwai (Ancient Clans)|2010}}</ref>

The rebellion escalated, but by the 22nd year (528?), Iwai was defeated by the imperial army under {{ill|Mononobe no Arakabi|en|Mononobe no Arakabi|qid=Q1114837|lt=Mononobe no Arakabi}} and killed in battle.<ref name="Nihon Shoki"/> His son, [[Tsukushi no Katsurako]], surrendered by offering the {{ill|Q24874980|ja|糟屋屯倉|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q24874980}} to the imperial court.<ref>{{Harv|Iwai (Ancient Clans)|2010}}</ref>

=== Chikugo no Kuni Fudoki ===
The {{ill|Chikugo no Kuni Fudoki|ja|筑後国風土記|qid=Q135597604}} describes Iwai's Kofun and records that he constructed it during his lifetime but abandoned it after losing his rebellion.<ref>{{Harv|Iwai (Ancient Clans)|2010}}</ref>

== Tomb ==
{{Gallery
|File:岩戸山古墳 石馬.jpg|Stone horse from Iwatoyama Kofun (on display at the Iwatoyama Historical Museum).
}}
The {{ill|Iwato-yama Kofun|ja|岩戸山古墳}}, identified as Iwai's tomb, is a {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|en|Zenpō-kōen-fun|qid=Q11268718|lt=Zenpō-kōen-fun}} in {{ill|Yame|en|Yame|qid=Q850492|lt=Yame, Fukuoka}}. The largest kofun in northern Kyushu, it dates to the early 6th century.<ref>{{Harv|Iwatoyama Historical Museum|2009}}</ref>

== Legacy ==
Iwai is considered a pivotal figure symbolizing early resistance to Yamato rule, with his tomb illustrating the wealth and power he wielded over northern Kyushu.<ref>{{Harv|Mizutani Chikashi|2013}}</ref>
